transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05 15:00 EDT
Duration: ~54 minutes (recording)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonas Reed (Redwood SE), Clara Zhou (CTO, Rivermark), Ethan Murphy (Head of Security), Priya Nair (Legal), Luis Gomez (Platform)

Auto-summary: Customer requires EU-only processing for EU customer PII, wants to understand Redwood's subprocessor chain and KMS key custody. They have strict DPA requirements and will need SOC2 artifacts. Agreed on pilot and follow-ups.

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ---
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're on the call to walk through territorial processing, subprocessor mapping and the KMS options. Jonas is with me on the technical side.
[00:12] Clara: Thanks, Maya. Quick context: Rivermark's product stores EU customer PII and our legal team requires processing & inference to happen in EU datacenters only. We also need to understand how Redwood handles subprocessors, like cloud infra and telemetry.
[00:25] Jonas: Totally, understood. Before we get deep, can I verify — is the requirement hard-block for processing in EU, or is it acceptable to have egress if it's encrypted and covered by contract?
[00:36] Ethan: It's pretty strict. For EU customers, inference + temporary KV/prefix cache must not leave EU. Metadata logs might be okay to replicate, but we need to map it out. Basically, no cross-border tokenization step.
[00:48] Maya: Got it. So policy we should treat as region-pin for both inference and KV cache. Our platform supports region affinity and strict routing. I'll let Jonas explain technical knobs.
[00:58] Jonas: Right — we have routing policies that can pin requests to a regional model pool. For EU pinning we serve off EU-hosted instances, and we also offer a private deployment in a VPC in customer region for stricter controls. There are tradeoffs: latency and cost. If you want on-prem like air-gapped, that's a different path.
[01:15] Luis: Do you have a list of subprocessors per region? We need to see where backups, logs, and monitoring live.
[01:22] Jonas: Yes, we maintain a subprocessor inventory. For hosted we use public cloud providers (redacted names in doc) and a CDN provider for blobs. Backups are stored in the same region by default; cross-region replication is opt-in.
[01:34] Priya: We need the actual contract language — where subprocessors are listed and the flow for notification on new subprocessors. Also, any possibility of data flowing to the US for model improvements?
[01:44] Maya: On model improvements, we have an option to opt-out of telemetry for accounts and also a default retention policy. For enterprise accounts we can configure retention windows and disable model improvement telemetry.
[01:55] Ethan: Ok but how do we prove it? Audit logs? We need tamper-evident logs showing request routing and storage locations.
[02:05] Jonas: We can emit per-request routing traces and persistent audit logs with location metadata. Logs can be ingested to your SIEM via syslog or S3 transfer in EU region only. We do have an audit trail export that includes model version, node ID, and region tag.
[02:20] Clara: Is that part of the standard console or is it an add-on?
[02:25] Maya: Audit export and longer retention is typically an add-on for enterprise plans, but we can scope it into the pilot.
[02:31] Ethan: What about encryption — where do keys live? If keys are in US KMS, that's a problem.
[02:36] Jonas: We support two primary approaches: Redwood-managed KMS with regional key stores, or BYOK using your KMS (KMS federation). For EU-pinned customers, we can place keys in EU HSMs and integrate with customer KMS via key import or through remote wrap/unwrap flows. Note: full BYOK with on-prem HSM may need Private deployment.
[02:55] Luis: For throughput, if we pin to EU, will that change the batching behaviour? Our peak comes at CET 9am and we need steady p50 latency.
[03:05] Jonas: Batching is workload-dependent; pinning doesn't change batching logic but it does limit available pool size unless you provision Dedicated capacity. We'll model throughput in the pilot; if you need SLOs at scale we recommend Redwood Dedicated reserved capacity in EU.
[03:20] Priya: Liability-wise, what indemnities do you offer for subprocessor breaches and notification times?
[03:27] Maya: Those are contractual items — typical DPA with subprocessors clause and 72-hour breach notification. We'll share our standard DPA redline and can negotiate specific SLAs.
[03:38] Clara: Can you confirm you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? Our procurement requires both.
[03:45] Maya: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified. I'll share the redacted reports after the call.
[03:52] Ethan: Great, we'll need the scope details — whether encryption key custody was in scope and whether subprocessors were enumerated in the audit.
[04:00] Jonas: I'll annotate the SOC 2 artifacts with where KMS and subprocessors were in scope.
[04:06] Maya: Quick note on cross-border: we discussed limiting processing to EU, but we may allow limited-metadata replication to US for analytics. We should clarify which fields are allowed.
[04:18] Priya: No PII in metadata replication. If metadata includes identifiers we need pseudonymization.
[04:24] Jonas: Understood. We can configure metadata filters in the pipeline to strip identifiable tokens before replication.
[04:30] Clara: About subprocessors — do you have an approval flow if a new subprocessor is added mid-contract?
[04:36] Maya: We provide 30 days notice for new subprocessors and a mechanism for customers to object; major objections can trigger mitigation plans or migration windows.
[04:45] Luis: On KMS — we use AWS KMS in eu-west-1. Do you integrate directly or do we need to do key import?
[04:52] Jonas: We support both; direct integration via AWS KMS grants (federated) is possible, or you can import wrapped keys. We'll need an ops-level runbook for the deep-dive.
[04:59] Ethan: Is there any scenario where model weights or training data leave the EU? Even ephemeral caches?
[05:05] Jonas: Model weights for open models are cached per region. We do not ship training data; inference-only. Ephemeral KV cache stays in region for EU pinned workloads. The only cross-border flows would be optional analytics exports or model improvement opt-in.
[05:20] Clara: Okay that helps. What about observability — if Redwood needs to troubleshoot, do you have playbooks to narrow scope without pulling data out?
[05:28] Maya: Yes, we have scoped access and session recording. For troubleshooting we can do live debugging in-region or request a sanitized trace export. We also support screen-shared debugging sessions into the private environment if you're on Private.
[05:42] Priya: On the DPA side we need the subprocessors mapped to contract clauses and a runbook for breach notification.
[05:49] Maya: We'll provide an annotated subprocessor inventory + DPA excerpt.
[05:53] Jonas: Also we'll include the model routing logs sample so you can see the per-request region tag.
[06:00] Clara: Pilot plan — we want a 2-week ingestion and inference pilot pinned to EU with our sample dataset. Success criteria: no cross-border egress, p95 latency below 350ms, and audit logs with region tags accessible. Is that feasible?
[06:14] Jonas: Feasible. We'll spin up an EU-pinned environment and set retention/telemetry to enterprise settings for that project. If you hit capacity we can add dedicated pool.
[06:24] Luis: We'll provide dataset and a low-level throughput profile.
[06:28] Maya: Great — next steps we'll share artifacts and schedule KMS deep dive. Any hard blockers?
[06:34] Priya: One more legal Q — subprocessors list must include subcontracting terms and whether subprocessors are allowed to engage others.
[06:42] Maya: Yes, we'll flag third-tier subprocessors in the inventory and provide contract language.
[06:47] Ethan: Regarding audit logs tamper evidence — do you support signed log chains or WORM storage?
[06:53] Jonas: We can stitch logs into a signed chain and export to an S3 bucket with Object Lock (WORM) in EU region. That meets tamper-evident requirement.
[07:03] Clara: Excellent. On timelines, procurement expects pilot contract by 2027-10-10. Can Redwood deliver artifacts before that?
[07:10] Maya: We'll aim to deliver SOC2 redactions and subprocessor inventory by 2027-10-08 so you can proceed.
[07:15] Jonas: I'll work on the technical attachments and pilot blueprint.
[07:19] Luis: We'll review and loop back with a shortlist of success metrics.
[07:23] Maya: Ok wrapping up — to recap: Redwood sends SOC 2/ISO summaries, subprocessor inventory, sample routing logs; schedule KMS deep-dive; kickoff EU-pinned 2-week pilot mid-Oct.
[07:36] Clara: Sounds good, thanks.
[07:39] Priya: Thanks all.
[07:41] Ethan: Thanks.

(There was some brief cross-talk around 00:38 where connection cut and Jonas repeated the KMS options, transcription may have slight word swaps.)

End of meeting.
